title: The Normal Distribution, Part 2
videoTitle: AP Statistics Topic 2.11 Part 2 The Normal Distribution
intro: After this lesson you can solve for a missing mean or standard deviation of a normal distribution from a given percent, and use the z-score formula and Desmos to find both when two percents are given.

moments.title: The harder normal problems
moments.text: Given some information about the scenario, you solve for the mean, the standard deviation, or both.

moments.title: Quiz scores: missing mean
moments.text: The SD is 6 and 84% score below 78. Find the z-score with 84% below it, then solve for $\mu$.

moments.title: The percent is the link
moments.text: Use the standard normal with mean 0 and SD 1 to turn the percent into a z-score, because the real mean is unknown.

moments.title: Solve the z-score formula for the mean
moments.text: Multiply by the SD, then solve for $\mu$. Watch the negative sign on $\mu$.

moments.title: Package weights: missing mean
moments.text: The SD is 1.5 and 2.5% of packages are over 18.5 pounds. The z-score is 1.96 and the mean is about 15.56.

moments.title: Follow-up: percent below 15 pounds
moments.text: Only after finding the mean can you find the z-score for 15 and the area, about 0.355.

moments.title: Test time: missing SD
moments.text: The mean is 70 and 3% finish in under 58 minutes. The z-score is $-1.881$ and the SD is about 6.38.

moments.title: Only possible because it is normal
moments.text: Without a statement that the variable is normally distributed, none of this work is valid.

moments.title: Tire lifetime: missing SD
moments.text: The mean is 45,000 miles and 16% last over 50,000. The SD is about 5,030 miles.

moments.title: Follow-up: between 40,000 and 55,000
moments.text: Find both z-scores and the area between them, about 0.816.

moments.title: SAT: both unknown
moments.text: 600 is the 50th percentile and 700 the 84th. The 50th percentile of a normal distribution is the mean.

moments.title: Two equations, two unknowns
moments.text: Put the known mean into the second equation and solve for the SD.

moments.title: Commute times: both unknown
moments.text: 6% below 20 minutes and 95% below 42 minutes give two z-scores and two equations.

moments.title: Solve each equation for the mean
moments.text: Set the two expressions for $\mu$ equal, solve for $\sigma$, then back-substitute for $\mu$.

moments.title: The statistics is the setup
moments.text: Most of the work is algebra. The new idea is turning each percent into a z-score.

moments.title: Follow-up: between 25 and 40 minutes
moments.text: With $\mu$ and $\sigma$ found, the area between the z-scores is about 0.708.

sections.title: What is missing, and what is the plan?

cards.name: Percent to z-score
cards.text: Every problem starts by turning a given percent into a z-score on the standard normal.

cards.name: One value, one z
cards.text: Put $x$, the z-score, and the known parameter into $z=\dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma}$ and solve.

notes.label: Wording check.
notes.text: Every one of these problems depends on the variable being approximately normal. State that before you use a z-score.

sections.title: Find a missing mean or standard deviation

questions.obj: Find a missing mean from a percentile
questions.q: Quiz scores are approximately normal with standard deviation 6. 84% of the scores are below 78. Find the mean score.

steps.t: Say that the variable is approximately normal and name what is unknown.

work.text: The mean $\mu$ is unknown and the standard deviation is 6.

steps.t: Find the $z$-score for the given percent on the standard normal.

work.text: 0.994 is the $z$-score with 84% of the standard normal to its left. The standard normal is used because $\mu$ is unknown.

steps.t: Substitute $x$, $z$, and the known standard deviation into the formula.

work.text: The value is 78 and the standard deviation is 6.
Multiply both sides by 6, then rearrange so that $\mu$ is on its own.

questions.answer: The mean quiz score is about 72.04 points.

questions.obj: Find a missing mean from a tail area
questions.q: The weights of packages shipped by a company are approximately normal with standard deviation 1.5 pounds. 2.5% of packages weigh more than 18.5 pounds. Find the mean weight.

steps.t: Say that the variable is approximately normal and name what is unknown.

work.text: The mean $\mu$ is unknown and the standard deviation is 1.5 pounds.

steps.t: Find the $z$-score for the given percent on the standard normal.

work.text: 1.96 is the $z$-score with 2.5% above it, which is 97.5% to its left.

steps.t: Substitute $x$, $z$, and the known standard deviation into the formula.

work.text: The value is 18.5 pounds and the standard deviation is 1.5 pounds.
Multiply both sides by 1.5, then rearrange so that $\mu$ is on its own.

questions.answer: The mean weight of the packages is 15.56 pounds.

sections.title: Find both the mean and the standard deviation

questions.obj: Find both the mean and the standard deviation
questions.q: Commute times are approximately normal. 6% of times are below 20 minutes and 95% are below 42 minutes. Find the mean and the standard deviation of the commute times.

steps.t: Find both $z$-scores on the standard normal.

work.text: $-1.555$ is the $z$-score with 6% to its left, and 1.645 is the $z$-score with 95% to its left.

steps.t: Write one $z$-score equation for each percent.

work.text: Each percent gives one equation, so there are two equations in two unknowns.

steps.t: Solve each equation for $\mu$, then set the two expressions equal.

work.text: Both expressions equal $\mu$, so setting them equal leaves an equation in $\sigma$ alone.
Either equation gives the same mean.

questions.answer: The mean commute time is about 30.69 minutes, and the standard deviation is about 6.875 minutes.

sections.title: Normal areas explorer
sections.intro: Check the facts behind each problem. With the mean and SD fixed, find the area for a value, or choose the area and read the value that marks it.

stories.quiz: Quiz scores are approximately normal with mean about 72 points and standard deviation 6 points. The explorer uses a whole-number mean of 72.
stories.commute: Commute times are approximately normal with mean about 31 minutes and standard deviation about 7 minutes. These are rounded from the video's values.

sections.title: Desmos walkthrough
sections.intro: The calculator starts empty. Work through each task in it yourself, the way you would on the exam, then check what you observe.

steps.title: z-score for a percent below
steps.suppose: 84% of scores are below 78 and we need the z-score.
steps.observe: The answer is a z-score, not a probability. It is positive because more than half the area is below it.
do: Keep [[Normal distribution]]. Enter 0 for mean and 1 for stdev, then press [[Create Distribution]].
Open [[Cumulative Probability]] and, under COMPUTE, choose [[Bounds]].

steps.title: z-score for a percent above
steps.observe: The z-score is positive, because only 2.5% of the area is above it.

steps.title: Area for a follow-up
steps.suppose: the mean is 15.56 and the SD is 1.5, and we want the percent of packages under 15 pounds.
steps.observe: Area gives a probability when you enter a value. Bounds gives a value when you enter a probability.
do: On a new row type `(15-15.56)/1.5` to get the z-score.
Under COMPUTE choose [[Area]], and under REGION choose [[Left]].
Enter that z-score in the box.

steps.title: z-score for a small percent
steps.suppose: 3% finish a test in under 58 minutes and the mean is 70.
steps.observe: The z-score is negative, because 3% is far below the center.

steps.title: Area between two z-scores
steps.suppose: tires have mean 45,000 and SD about 5,030 miles, and we want the proportion that last between 40,000 and 55,000 miles.
steps.observe: Check that the shaded area is mostly the middle of the curve.
do: Under COMPUTE choose [[Area]], and under REGION choose [[Inner]].
Enter the two z-scores as the lower and upper bounds.

steps.title: Two z-scores for two percents
steps.suppose: 6% of commute times are below 20 minutes and 95% are below 42 minutes.
steps.observe: The first z-score is negative and the second is positive.
do: With [[Bounds]] chosen on the standard normal, under REGION choose [[Left]].
Enter 0.06 and read the first z-score.
Change the area to 0.95 and read the second z-score.

sections.title: Write it so it earns credit

traps.title: Using the problem's mean and SD when one is unknown
traps.weak: Typed a guessed mean into Desmos to find the area.
traps.better: Use the standard normal (mean 0, SD 1) with Bounds to get the z-score from the percent, then solve the z-score formula for the missing parameter.

traps.title: Wrong sign on the z-score for a percent above
traps.better: 2.5% above means 97.5% below, so the z-score is $+1.96$. Use the right option, or the left option with 0.975.

traps.title: State that the model is normal
traps.better: Because test times are approximately normal, the 3% below 58 minutes gives $z=-1.881$. Then $\sigma=\frac{58-70}{-1.881}\approx6.38$ minutes.

traps.title: Mixing up a z-score with the original value
traps.better: 0.84 is the area below 78, not a z-score. The z-score for that area is 0.994, and that goes in the formula.

questions.stem: Exam scores are approximately normal with $\sigma=10$. 90% of scores are below 82. Which equation can be solved for $\mu$?
why: 0.90 is an area, not a z-score.
The z-score for 90% below is positive.
The z-score with 90% below is 1.282. It goes in $z=\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}$ with $x=82$.
The numerator is reversed, which flips the sign.

questions.stem: 15% of the values of a normal variable are above $x$. Which z-score goes with $x$?
why: That is the z-score with 15% below.
0.15 is an area, not a z-score.
0.85 is an area, not a z-score.

questions.stem: The weights of bags are approximately normal with $\sigma=2$ ounces. 5% of bags weigh less than 40 ounces. What is the mean?
why: That subtracts $z\sigma$ with $z=-1.645$, which moves the wrong way.
That is the same as the first value with the sign flipped.

questions.stem: A normal variable has 50% below 600 and 84% below 700. Which statement is true?
why: The 50th percentile is the mean. Then $0.994=\frac{700-600}{\sigma}$ gives $\sigma\approx100.6$.
The mean is the 50th percentile, not the midpoint of the two values.
700 has a z-score of 0.994. It is not the mean.
0.994 is a z-score, not the SD.

sections.title: Write a full response
sections.prompt: The waiting time at a clinic is approximately normally distributed with a standard deviation of 8 minutes. 90% of patients wait less than 35 minutes.
parts: (b) Find the proportion of patients who wait less than 20 minutes.
(c) At a second clinic the waiting time is also approximately normal. 10% of patients wait less than 12 minutes and 75% wait less than 30 minutes. Find the mean and standard deviation.
sample: (a) The z-score with 90% below it is 1.282. $1.282=\frac{35-\mu}{8}$, so $\mu=35-1.282(8)\approx24.74$ minutes.
(b) $z=\frac{20-24.74}{8}\approx-0.593$. $P(Z<-0.593)\approx0.277$. About 27.7% of patients wait less than 20 minutes.

(c) The z-scores are $z_1=-1.282$ for 10% below and $z_2=0.674$ for 75% below. $-1.282=\frac{12-\mu}{\sigma}$ and $0.674=\frac{30-\mu}{\sigma}$. Subtracting, $1.956\sigma=18$, so $\sigma\approx9.20$ minutes. Then $\mu=12+1.282(9.20)\approx23.80$ minutes.
checklist: (a) Solves for the mean, about 24.74 minutes, with units
(b) Finds the z-score for 20 using the new mean
(c) Two z-scores from the two percents, two equations, and both parameters solved, mean about 23.80 and SD about 9.20

In the tire follow-up the captions say 50,000 where the upper bound is 55,000. The page uses 55,000.
